rationale: All twelve blocking findings from code-review-final.json are accounted for: ten verified as code fixes read at current HEAD 7133a5a5a (collision-aware and defensive custom-field name resolution with a strict AmbiguousCustomFieldException that subclasses InvalidCustomFieldException, the ADF null-content guard, strict validation on the PUT route, the endpoint return annotation, the modern annotations on every added source line, and the four missing test layers at processor, model, route and health-check), and two closed on recorded owner decisions with outcome and rationale rather than code changes. Confidence is medium, not high, because CR-004 and CR-012 were typed 'code' by the prior verdict but resolved on decision evidence: CR-004's lenient warn-and-skip remains in source with its remedy deferred to a separate EPMCDME ticket, and commit 7d6b8f4d4 'Sonar fix' still carries no ticket prefix, mitigated only by the squash-merge strategy. business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged; standards_path is null by contract for this round, so no coverage gap is recorded.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; 4 of 7 subjects conform, but 'Sonar fix' carries no ticket prefix and no colon. The two git-generated merge subjects are collapsed by the documented squash-merge strategy and are not counted.

Two code-quality.md 'Types And Imports' rules unmet in new code: typing.Optional/List generics instead of 'X | None' and 'list[...]', and the new endpoint get_jira_datasource_fields has no return annotation. License headers present; no new source files.

New GET /v1/index/jira/fields relies on the router-level Depends(authenticate); creds resolved via the central SettingsService lookup, adding no access path. No token/key/header logged. custom_fields matched strictly against the Jira field catalogue, and the outbound 'fields' param is assembled only from server-returned ids.
